comparisons.peer_summary: UTB balances affecting the effective tax rate were $573 million at December 31, 2024, with a possible decrease of up to $217 million in the next 12 months. The Corporation recognized an interest benefit of $9 million in 2024 and had accruals for interest and penalties of $105 million at year-end 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC disclose a reasonable possibility of significant changes in unrecognized tax benefits (UTB) within the next 12 months but differ in the specificity of their estimates. MS explicitly states it is not possible to reasonably estimate the expected change or its impact on the effective tax rate. In contrast, BAC provides a specific quantitative estimate, stating the UTB balance may decrease by as much as $217 million, and quantifies the UTB balance affecting the effective tax rate at $573 million.

sentences.text: It is reasonably possible that significant changes in the balance of unrecognized tax benefits may occur within the next 12 months.

At this time, however, it is not possible to reasonably estimate the expected change to the total amount of unrecognized tax benefits and the impact on the Firm's effective tax rate over the next 12 months.

At December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, the balance of the Corporation's UTBs which would, if recognized, affect the Corporation's effective tax rate was $573 million, $671 million and $709 million, respectively.

It is reasonably possible that the UTB balance may decrease by as much as $217 million during the next 12 months, since resolved items will be removed from the balance whether their resolution results in payment or recognition.
